patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2020 and had three babies (2022, 2024, 2026). Her postpartum years carry postpartum thyroiditis and depression after the first, mastitis, IPV disclosure and lactational amenorrhea after the second, and endometritis with septic pelvic thrombophlebitis, recurrent postpartum depression on sertraline, recurrent mastitis and an LNG-IUD after the third.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sheila is 30, new to the practice. Teaches second grade in South Hadley. Lives with her partner. Old PCP retired; last physical about two years ago, last Pap she thinks around 2017 and normal.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations. PSH: none. Never pregnant. Meds: none, no supplements. NKDA.
FH: mother has rheumatoid arthritis. Father healthy as far as she knows. No known family history of early heart disease or cancer.
SH: never smoked. Alcohol maybe once a month, a glass of wine. No drugs. Walks most evenings. Feels safe at home.

ROS: negative across systems; periods regular, monthly, not heavy.

Exam: BP and pulse in the vitals tab. BMI ~22. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid smooth, not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts symmetric, no masses. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected. Skin no rashes. Mood bright.

A/P: healthy 30 y/o establishing care.
- Screening: Pap with HPV today. One-time HIV and hep C, she agrees. CBC, CMP, lipids.
- Vaccines: flu shot when the clinic doses arrive in early October. Tdap she believes was 2015; will look in old records.
- PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C low.
- Asked about future pregnancy: thinking about it in the next year or two.
Return yearly.

documents.title: Your lab and Pap results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sheila, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Your Pap was normal and the HPV test was negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Good to meet you. Text me if anything comes up.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, LABOR AND DELIVERY
Admission 09/04/2022, discharge 09/06/2022.

G1 now P1, 31 y/o, admitted in spontaneous labor at 39 weeks after an uncomplicated prenatal course. Prenatal labs unremarkable; Tdap given 07/2022 at the OB office.
Spontaneous vaginal delivery 09/05/2022 of a healthy infant. EBL within normal. Postpartum course routine; afebrile; breastfeeding well with lactation support.
Discharge medications: ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit in 6 weeks.

Received by fax. Filed to chart, PCP aware.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day visit: palpitations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning; worked in at 11:20.

S: Baby is 7.5 weeks, vaginal delivery 9/5, breastfeeding without trouble. Since yesterday her heart has been racing on and off, she feels hot when nobody else is, keyed up, and couldn't fall asleep last night even when the baby did. No chest pain, no syncope, no shortness of breath. No fever, no sore throat, no neck pain. Not taking anything, no decongestants, coffee one cup. Mood ok, "just wired."

O: HR 108 regular. Afebrile. Fine tremor of outstretched hands. Thyroid not tender, not enlarged. No exophthalmos or lid lag. Heart tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Warm moist skin.

A/P: Postpartum, new adrenergic symptoms, tremor, tachycardia. Leading concern is postpartum thyroiditis in the thyrotoxic phase; an autoimmune hyperthyroidism is less likely but needs to be excluded.
- TSH and free T4 today, stat. CBC.
- If abnormal, endocrinology this week; she prefers someone who will work around breastfeeding.
- Return precautions: chest pain, fainting, fever.

Addendum 16:55: TSH 0.02, free T4 2.4. Called her; endocrinology agreed to see her Monday 10/31. Referral faxed with labs.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily as needed for palpitations or tremor

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP
Consultation, date of service 10/31/2022
Referring: primary care, membership internal medicine

Reason for consult: thyrotoxicosis 8 weeks postpartum.

History: 32-year-old teacher, first baby delivered vaginally eight weeks ago after a full-term pregnancy without complications. Nursing well. For four days she has felt warm, anxious and on edge, with frequent palpitations, poor sleep, and sweating in rooms others find comfortable. Appetite up a little; weight unchanged by her report. No sore throat or recent viral illness. Takes no medications. Allergies: none known.
Family history: she knows of no thyroid disease in the family. Mother has rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, about once a month. Teaches elementary school.

Exam: temperature 98.6 F, pulse 112, BP 120/76. Fine tremor of both hands. Thyroid gland normal in size, nontender, no nodules. No proptosis, lid retraction or periorbital change.

Data: outside TSH 0.02 mIU/L and free T4 2.4 ng/dL (10/28). Today free T3 6.1 pg/mL, TPO antibody 210 IU/mL, TSH receptor antibody 0.8 IU/L (negative).

Impression: painless postpartum thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase. The negative receptor antibody, nontender normal-sized gland, absent eye findings and timing all favor it over autoimmune hyperthyroidism. A radioiodine uptake study would confirm low uptake but would mean interrupting breastfeeding; we agreed to defer it since the labs answer the question.

Plan:
1. Propranolol 10 mg up to three times a day for palpitations and tremor; compatible with nursing. Stop once symptoms settle.
2. No antithyroid drug; it does not help this phase.
3. TSH and free T4 in about 6 weeks through primary care, then every 6 to 8 weeks for the first postpartum year, watching for a hypothyroid swing.
4. Positive TPO antibody raises the long-term risk of hypothyroidism; yearly TSH after recovery and a check after any future delivery.

Thank you for the referral.

Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Propranolol and nursing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The endocrinologist said propranolol is fine with breastfeeding but my mother-in-law is worried. I've been taking it twice a day and it really helps the pounding. Is it ok to keep going?

documents.title: RE: Propranolol and nursing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, keep going. Very little gets into milk at that dose and it's one of the preferred choices for nursing mothers. Watch the baby for unusual sleepiness, which would be rare. Bloodwork around December 12 and we'll see if you can come off it.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here with baby in carrier. Breastfeeding, both vaccines safe while nursing, reviewed. Flu quadrivalent L deltoid, Pfizer bivalent booster R deltoid. Says palpitations much less, using propranolol about once a day now. Observed 15 min, fine.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: thyroiditis, mood
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Lab drawn before the visit; TSH 0.9 and free T4 1.3 already back.

Thyroid: palpitations gone for about two weeks, hasn't needed propranolol in 10 days. Tremor gone. Sleeping when she can.

Mood: when I asked how she was really doing she teared up. For about 3–4 weeks: low most days, crying in the car on the way back to the house, guilt that she isn't enjoying the baby the way she expected, worrying constantly, lying awake after night feeds. Still caring for the baby well, eating, partner helping some. Denies any thoughts of harming herself or the baby. No prior depression before this year. Planning to return to school in January.
PHQ-9 14, GAD-7 8.

Exam: pulse normal, regular. Tearful, organized, good eye contact. Thyroid normal. Tremor absent.

A/P:
1. Postpartum thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase, resolving. Stop propranolol. TSH/free T4 again mid-February, then spring. Told her a low-thyroid phase can follow (tired, cold, constipated) and to tell me.
2. Postpartum depression, moderate. Discussed therapy and medication; she wants to start with therapy and is open to meds if not better. Referral to the perinatal psychiatry clinic, they also run a therapy group. Postpartum support line number given. Safety plan reviewed; she will text or call if any thoughts of self-harm.
Check-in by phone in 2 weeks; see her in about 6 weeks.

documents.title: Mood check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called per PCP. Intake call done with the perinatal psychiatry clinic, first appointment Jan 5. Says the holidays were hard but her mother has been staying with them. No thoughts of self-harm. Knows to text PCP or go to the ED if that changes.

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PERINATAL MENTAL HEALTH CLINIC, outside psychiatry group
Initial evaluation, date of service 01/05/2023

ID: 32 y/o G1P1, 4 months postpartum, elementary teacher due back in the classroom later this month. Referred by her PCP.

HPI: Low mood and anxious rumination starting roughly 10 weeks after delivery, overlapping with the end of a thyrotoxic phase of postpartum thyroiditis (now treated and normalizing per PCP labs). Tearful most days, guilt about not feeling the attachment she expected, insomnia beyond infant waking. Function preserved. Denies suicidal ideation, past or present; denies intrusive thoughts of harming the infant. No mania, no psychosis. No prior psychiatric history, no prior treatment.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: lives with partner and infant; her mother helps several days a week. Alcohol rare, never smoker. Breastfeeding.

MSE: casually dressed, cooperative, mood "flat and guilty," affect constricted and tearful at times, thought process linear, no SI/HI, insight and judgment good.

Assessment: Postpartum depression, moderate, first episode. Low acute risk.

Plan: weekly individual CBT with our clinic therapist; she prefers to hold medication, which is reasonable at this severity, and we will revisit an SSRI compatible with breastfeeding if no improvement in 6–8 weeks. Safety plan completed. Return in 6 weeks.

cc: primary care

documents.title: TSH result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH 3.6, free T4 1.0. Within range, TSH drifting up as expected after the thyrotoxic phase. She reports energy ok, no cold intolerance. Repeat with June visit. Portal message sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from April (school concert week).

Mood: finished 14 weeks of CBT at the perinatal clinic last month; psychiatry discharged her back to us. Feels like herself, enjoying the baby, sleeping in longer stretches now that the baby does. Back at work since January and it went better than expected. PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 2. No SI.

Thyroid: no symptoms either direction.

Family history update: she asked her mother after the endocrinology visit, and her mother was told years ago she has autoimmune thyroiditis; never treated as far as she knows. Added.

Exam: well, bright affect. Thyroid normal, no tremor. HR 70s.

A/P:
- Postpartum depression, recovered. Moved to history. Higher chance of recurrence after a future birth; she and her OB should plan for close mood follow-up next time.
- Postpartum thyroiditis, recovered; TSH today 2.1 (resulted after visit, normal). TPO positive, maternal thyroiditis: TSH yearly and after any future delivery.
- Pap/HPV next 2025. Flu in the fall.
See her for a physical when ready; she is thinking about a second baby.

documents.title: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know I'm pregnant again, about 6 weeks. Seeing the same OB group next week. Anything I should tell them given the thyroid and the depression last time?

documents.title: RE: News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, two things: ask them to check a TSH early in the pregnancy and again after delivery because of the thyroiditis and the TPO antibody, and let them know about the postpartum depression so they can screen you closely after the birth. I'll send them a summary with your permission. Reply yes and I'll fax it today.

documents.title: RE: RE: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yes please, thank you.

documents.title: OB/GYN Office Visit: mastitis
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, office visit 05/09/2024

33-year-old P2, two weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal birth, exclusively nursing. Two days of a painful, swollen left breast with tiredness and chills. Feeding on that side hurts. Baby has begun clamping down/biting during feeds. Past history of postpartum depression and postpartum thyroiditis (endocrinology, 2022).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal autoimmune thyroiditis; mother with RA.
Tobacco never; alcohol rare.

Temp 38.4 C (101.1 F).
Breasts: left upper outer quadrant erythematous, warm, firm and tender. Left nipple with a fissure. No fluctuance, no discharge. Right breast unremarkable.

Assessment: lactational mastitis, left, likely entry through the nipple fissure.
Plan: dicloxacillin 500 mg QID x 10 days. Keep emptying the breast, feed or pump from the left. Ibuprofen for pain and fever. Nipple care for the fissure; lactation consultant appointment for latch and the biting. Call for a mass, spreading redness or no improvement in 48 hours.

Faxed to PCP.

documents.title: Breast infection
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI the OB put me on dicloxacillin for mastitis yesterday. Fever already broke. The baby seems fine with it. Just making sure you knew.

documents.title: RE: Breast infection
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Sheila, the doctor saw the OB's note and is glad you're feeling better. Finish all 10 days. We'd like to see you after your six-week OB visit, can you do mid-June after school?

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, postpartum visit 06/04/2024

Six weeks after an uncomplicated SVD. Mastitis treated last month and cleared. She says she is overwhelmed with a newborn and a toddler. More frequent arguments with her partner lately; on questioning she says she sometimes feels frightened when the partner has been drinking. Denies being hit, pushed or threatened with harm. Feels worn out and cut off from friends. Infant healthy, nursing well. No bleeding concerns, no fever.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits. Tired-appearing, otherwise well. Breasts normal, no residual induration. Abdomen soft. Perineum healed. Uterus involuted.

Assessment:
1. Routine postpartum exam, normal.
2. Intimate partner violence, emotional, disclosed today. No physical harm reported. She is not in immediate danger by her account and does not want to leave the home.
Plan: private discussion of safety, a domestic violence hotline card and the local advocacy program number given; she has a safe person (her mother). Encouraged follow-up with her PCP this month. Contraception discussed; she declines a method for now and plans to nurse.

cc PCP

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Postpartum follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen alone; baby with her mother in the waiting room.

Read the OB note from 6/4. She confirms: the two of them have been fighting more since the baby, and it's worse on nights when the partner drinks. Arguments get loud. Never hit, shoved or threatened. No weapons in the home. Partner is not violent with the children per her. She doesn't want to leave and says things are calmer most weeks. Has the hotline card and her mother knows.

Mood: tired, stretched thin, but not the same as 2022. Enjoying the baby. PHQ-9 6, item 9 zero. Sleep broken by feeds only.
Thyroid: no symptoms. Breast: fully better after the antibiotic.

Exam: pulse normal. Weight up from prepregnancy, expected. Calm, appropriate, a bit tearful when talking about home. Thyroid normal.

A/P:
1. Intimate partner violence, emotional, by her report; no physical harm. Safety reviewed: safe person, keeps phone charged, knows to call 911 if threatened. Offered a counselor through the advocacy program; she wants to hold off. I'll ask at every visit, privately.
2. Mood: mild symptoms, monitor; low threshold to bring the perinatal clinic back in.
3. History of postpartum thyroiditis: TSH today (1.9, normal; message sent).
4. Mastitis resolved.
Physical early next year.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Trivalent flu, L deltoid, 0.5 mL IM. Nursing, no contraindication. Declined COVID this year, may do it later. No reaction.

documents.title: GYN Visit: amenorrhea
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, visit 12/09/2024

CC: no menstrual period in 6 months.
HPI: P2, baby nearly 8 months old, exclusively breastfed since birth. No period since the postpartum bleeding stopped. History of postpartum depression and postpartum thyroiditis; mastitis this spring.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Sexual/contraception: not sexually active since the birth; no contraceptive method.
ROS: no hot flashes, no vaginal dryness, libido unchanged.
Exam: BMI in the normal range. General and pelvic exam unremarkable.
Labs: prolactin 29 ng/mL (4–23), FSH 3.2 mIU/mL (3.5–12.5), LH 2.1 mIU/mL (2.4–12.6), TSH 2.5 mIU/L (0.4–4.0), estradiol 45 pg/mL (30–400).
Assessment: lactational amenorrhea. Mildly raised prolactin and low-normal gonadotropins fit ongoing nursing. Thyroid normal.
Plan: reassurance. Expect menses to return within a few months of weaning or reducing feeds. Return if no period 3 months after weaning, or if she resumes intercourse and wants contraception.

cc PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o here for her yearly exam before school.

Interval: weaned the baby in January. First period came about three weeks later, normal flow. Mastitis last spring, resolved. Saw OB in December for the missing periods, labs consistent with nursing.
Mood: good. PHQ-9 4. Sleeping better since the baby sleeps through.
Home: asked privately. Fewer arguments this winter; still never physically hurt or threatened. Safety plan and hotline number still in her phone. Declines counseling referral again, knows the offer stands.
Meds: none. NKDA. Never smoker, alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals fine. Thyroid normal size, nontender. Heart regular without murmur, lungs clear to bases. Abdomen soft. Breasts without masses. Skin unremarkable. Affect warm.

A/P: health maintenance, 34F.
- Lactational amenorrhea resolved with weaning; off the list.
- History of postpartum thyroiditis, TPO+: TSH today.
- History of postpartum depression: stable.
- IPV: as above, ongoing, will keep asking.
- Cervical screening due this year; she'd rather have it with OB at her next gyn visit. Will track.
- CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu given in October.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sheila, your blood counts, chemistries, cholesterol and thyroid all came back in the normal range. TSH 2.2. Nothing to change. Enjoy the rest of February vacation week!

documents.body: Surprise, positive test this weekend. Period was April 15 I think. Going back to the same OB group. Please send them my thyroid and mood history again?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant

documents.body: Congratulations. Summary and last TSH faxed to the OB office this morning. Remind them about the postpartum mood screening and a TSH after delivery. Since you'll be due in January, plan for flu and COVID shots here in the fall.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL MATERNITY SERVICE
Admitted 01/20/2026, discharged 01/23/2026.

35 y/o, now P3 (two prior vaginal births). Prenatal course uncomplicated; Tdap 11/2025.
Primary low transverse cesarean section 01/20/2026; healthy female infant. Postoperative course routine, afebrile at discharge, incision clean, tolerating diet, breastfeeding.
History: postpartum thyroiditis and postpartum depression after the first birth; IPV disclosure 2024 noted in prenatal record.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: ibuprofen, acetaminophen.

events.reason: postpartum fever and lower abdominal pain

medications.drug_text: 0.8 ML enoxaparin sodium 100 MG/ML Prefilled Syringe
medications.sig: Inject 80 mg under the skin every 12 hours for 14 days

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging. Postpartum uterus, enlarged as expected 10 days after cesarean delivery, with a thin endometrial stripe and no retained products. Lower uterine segment incision site without a fluid collection. Ovaries normal in size and appearance bilaterally. No adnexal mass. No free fluid. No abscess.
reports.conclusion: No pelvic abscess or retained products of conception.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, OBSTETRIC INPATIENT SERVICE
Admitted 01/25/2026 via the emergency department; discharged 02/03/2026.

Reason for admission: fever and lower abdominal pain starting postoperative day 5 after primary cesarean on 01/20.
ED: febrile, uterine tenderness; diagnosed with postpartum endometritis and admitted to OB on IV clindamycin and gentamicin.

Hospital course: Fever continued despite antibiotics. On 01/30 (postoperative day 10), temperature 38.9 C (102 F), HR 110, BP 120/75. No cough, dysuria or diarrhea. Lower abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding; fundal and bilateral adnexal tenderness on pelvic exam. WBC 15,000/mm3, hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, platelets 250,000/mm3, INR 1.0, PTT 30 seconds. Pelvic ultrasound without abscess or retained tissue. Blood cultures without growth. With persistent fever on appropriate antibiotics and no abscess, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis was diagnosed and a heparin infusion begun on 01/30. Afebrile within 48 hours. Antibiotics stopped after 48 hours afebrile; transitioned to enoxaparin.

Discharge diagnoses: puerperal septic thrombophlebitis; postpartum endometritis, treated.
Discharge medications: enoxaparin 80 mg subcutaneously every 12 hours for 14 days, then stop. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Breastfeeding throughout; enoxaparin compatible.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

Received by fax 2/5.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called within 2 business days of discharge. Home since Tuesday. No fever since the weekend before discharge, checking twice a day. Incision dry. Doing the enoxaparin shots herself, some bruising at sites, no other bleeding. Nursing the baby. Has enough syringes for the course. Appointment with PCP Tues 2/10 at 10:30. Mood: "exhausted." Partner home this week and her mother coming daily.

orders.reason: postpartum mood monitoring, history of postpartum depression

documents.title: Hospital follow-up (TCM)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with the baby, 3 weeks old.

Course reviewed from both discharge summaries: primary cesarean 1/20, readmitted 1/25 with endometritis, fever persisted on clindamycin/gentamicin, ultrasound without abscess, treated as septic pelvic thrombophlebitis with heparin and fever broke within two days. Home 2/3 on enoxaparin 80 mg q12h x 14 days, ends around 2/17.

Now: no fever at home for 10 days. Incision sore only with lifting. Lochia light. Some bruising at injection sites, no gum or other bleeding. Breastfeeding, baby gaining. Leg pain or swelling none, breathing fine.
Mood: tired and teary at times, feels behind on everything; not the dark place of 2022 "yet." PHQ-9 9, no thoughts of harming herself.
Home: partner on leave this week; no new concerns about safety when asked privately.

Exam: afebrile, pulse normal. Low transverse incision healing, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness at incision only. Calves soft, nontender. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis after endometritis: clinically resolved infection; complete 14 days of enoxaparin, then stop. Endometritis treated. RN to call 2/17.
2. Hb 11.5 today, up from 11.2 in hospital; expected after delivery and infection, recheck in a few months.
3. Mood: given the 2022 episode, re-referring to the perinatal psychiatry clinic now rather than waiting. Safety plan reviewed.
4. History of postpartum thyroiditis: TSH at about 6 weeks postpartum (OB or psychiatry may draw; will check results).
5. IPV: asked privately, no new concerns.
OB at 6 weeks. Text anytime.

medications.drug_text: 0.8 ML enoxaparin sodium 100 MG/ML Prefilled Syringe

documents.title: Enoxaparin course
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Last enoxaparin injection this morning, course complete per discharge plan and PCP. Removed from med list. Afebrile. Sharps container drop-off info given. Intake with perinatal psychiatry set for 3/4.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical specimen, satisfactory, endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit and IUD Insertion
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, 03/02/2026

Six weeks after primary cesarean, course complicated by endometritis and septic pelvic thrombophlebitis, now off enoxaparin and afebrile. Incision healed. Breastfeeding. Mood: tired, appointment with perinatal psychiatry this week. Wants long-acting contraception.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Incision well healed. Speculum: cervix normal; cotesting collected (due). Bimanual: uterus involuted, nontender, no adnexal tenderness or masses.

Procedure: levonorgestrel 52 mg IUD inserted after consent, sounding 7 cm, uncomplicated, strings trimmed to 3 cm. Tolerated well.

Plan: string check in 6 weeks or by self-check; expect irregular light bleeding for a few months. Pap/HPV results to patient and PCP.

Addendum 3/5: Pap NILM, HPV negative.

cc PCP

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry: return evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PERINATAL MENTAL HEALTH CLINIC
Return evaluation, date of service 03/04/2026

35-year-old seen here in 2023 for a first postpartum depressive episode (CBT, full recovery), now 6 weeks after the birth of her third child, a girl, by cesarean. Recently recovered from septic pelvic thrombophlebitis. Pregnancy itself was uncomplicated. PCP re-referred.

Since the delivery: sad most of the day, drained, overwhelmed. Lies awake when the baby is asleep. Lost interest in what she used to like, including time with the baby, and feels she is failing as a mother. Appetite down a lot; reports about 10 lb lost since delivery. She acknowledges thoughts of harming herself over the past two weeks, passive and some active, without a plan or intent, no preparatory acts; no thoughts of harming the children. No psychosis.
Meds: none (enoxaparin finished). Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, alcohol rare.
Safety: partner in the home; prior emotional IPV disclosed to OB 2024, she reports no physical violence. Mother lives nearby and is helping daily. No firearms.

Vitals within normal limits. Tired-appearing, otherwise unremarkable. MSE: tearful, mood "empty," affect constricted, linear, passive and intermittent active SI without plan or intent, future-oriented around her children, insight good.
Labs today: TSH 2.5 mIU/L, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, fasting glucose 88 mg/dL.

Assessment: postpartum depression, recurrent episode, with thoughts of self-harm. Thyroid normal; not anemic. Risk: elevated chronic, moderate acute; outpatient care appropriate with protective factors and safety plan.

Plan: start sertraline 50 mg daily (preferred during breastfeeding). Weekly therapy, first session this week. Written safety plan with her mother as support; crisis line and 988 reviewed; she agrees to go to the ED if intent emerges. Return in 2 weeks for medication check, sooner prn.

cc primary care

documents.title: Check-in after psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the psychiatry note, called her at lunch. Started sertraline Thursday, mild nausea only. Has the written safety plan on the fridge, her mother is at the house most days and her partner knows about the appointment. No intent to harm herself, would call 988 or go to the ED. Therapy session yesterday. Asked her to text me any day it gets worse. Added postpartum depression and sertraline to our list. Will see her in the late spring.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth four times daily for 10 days

documents.title: OB/GYN Visit: mastitis
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, 04/02/2026

35 y/o nursing a 2-month-old. Two days of fever, achiness and a sore left breast. Started shortly after she switched to a different hold/positioning technique she read about. Left-sided mastitis 2024. Also history of postpartum depression, on sertraline through psychiatry. IUD in place.
Allergies: NKDA.

Temp 38.5 C (101.3 F). Left breast: upper outer quadrant red and indurated, tender to touch; tender enlarged left axillary nodes. No fluctuant mass. Remainder of exam unremarkable.
CBC: WBC 11.8, mild leukocytosis.

Assessment: recurrent lactational mastitis, left.
Plan: cephalexin 500 mg QID x 10 days, continue nursing/pumping, cold compresses, ibuprofen. Back to her prior positioning; lactation follow-up. Breast ultrasound if a mass persists after treatment.

cc PCP

documents.title: Mastitis again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got mastitis again last week, OB put me on cephalexin. Fever gone since Saturday. The sertraline is starting to help I think, sleeping a little more. Just checking that cephalexin and sertraline are ok together.

documents.title: RE: Mastitis again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry about the mastitis, glad the fever's down. Yes, those two are fine together and both fine for the baby. Finish the full 10 days. Really glad sleep is a little better.

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry: follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PERINATAL MENTAL HEALTH CLINIC, follow-up 05/11/2026

Now about 10 weeks on sertraline 50 mg. Mood clearly better over the last month, sleeping when the baby sleeps, appetite back, enjoying the children again. No thoughts of self-harm for over a month. Nausea resolved. Weekly therapy continues; she finds it useful. Mastitis in April, treated by OB.
MSE: brighter, reactive affect, no SI/HI.
Assessment: postpartum depression, improving on sertraline.
Plan: continue sertraline 50 mg daily; we will continue to prescribe. Therapy every week to every other week. Return in 6 weeks.

cc PCP

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four and a half months after the cesarean. Came straight from school, baby with her mother.

Mood: real improvement since April. Sertraline 50 mg via psychiatry, weekly-ish therapy. Sleeping, eating, laughing again. No thoughts of harming herself since early April. PHQ-9 6, GAD-7 4.
Breast: finished cephalexin, no recurrence. Still nursing morning and night.
Pelvic: IUD in, spotting tapered off. No fevers since February. No leg swelling.
Home: asked alone. No physical harm or threats. Safety plan unchanged.
Weight down about 6 kg since February, appetite normal now, not dieting.

Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily, LNG-IUD. NKDA.
Exam: well, brighter than February. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Incision well healed. No calf tenderness.

A/P:
1. Postpartum depression, recurrent, improving on sertraline. Psychiatry managing dose; keep it going at least 6–12 months after remission.
2. Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis, resolved; anticoagulation done. Off the active list.
3. Mastitis x2, resolved.
4. History of postpartum thyroiditis: TSH and CBC today.
5. IPV: ongoing emotional, will keep asking. Hotline and advocacy numbers re-offered.
6. Contraception: LNG-IUD via OB.
Flu and COVID vaccines in the fall; physical after that.

documents.title: Monday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thyroid 1.8, normal, and your blood count is back to normal, so the anemia from the winter has corrected. Good to see you doing so much better. Have a great end of the school year.

documents.title: GYN Follow-up
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP, 07/28/2026

Routine follow-up. History: postpartum thyroiditis, postpartum depression, lactational amenorrhea 2024. Cesarean January 2026. No complaints today. Since the IUD went in this March she had a little light spotting for some weeks, which stopped; no period at all in the 6 months since delivery. No bleeding, discharge or pelvic pain. Wonders if not having periods is a problem.
Meds: levonorgestrel IUD. No other medications.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal autoimmune thyroiditis; mother with RA.

Vitals normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic exam unremarkable; strings visible.
Not anemic and TSH in range per recent outside labs. Pap normal in March.

Assessment: amenorrhea with levonorgestrel IUD, expected; no concern.
Plan: reassurance. Device good for several years. Return yearly or as needed.

cc PCP. Received 8/3, scanned, filed.
